title: Ridgley as a rock and roll artist
summary: He was a rock and roll artist, played white colleges across the region, and had a sing-along act with his band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well, getting back, did you ever think of yourself as a rock and roll star? As a rock and roll artist? Yeah, yeah. You did?

Typical, I was a rock and roll artist. See, When I Meet My Girl was defined as the first rockabilly tune to be the hit. You know, because it was a national record. And it was the first rockabilly. And from there, you know, I was strictly rock and roll. See, I played all of the white colleges. What could we talk about? I played from here, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Alabama. I played all of them. And it was strictly, you know, rock and roll. We did some of the, like, What I Say, Oop-Oop-A-Doo, was the tunes. But, you know, another thing that I started was the, what we used to call it, you know, when you gather all the audience around you and we would sing. What did they call them? Sing-along? No, not the sing-along. They had another name for it. Big, it was all over the country. But, you see, there were things that my band used to do. See, when, and it was, this was a time, a lot. See, I had to be playing about an hour or so. This, you know, everybody would, what I call everybody gather around and, you know, sit down on the floor and sit down straight around the band. And we would do the sing-along band. Oh. See, this was, I had that good band. Justin, Adam, and Emma, we'd go right into things. And, oh, I've got to think of this. But, anyway, those were the kind of things that kept me working. See, I had, we had a good act. And I had no other singer but me. It was a perfect, we had a perfect act.
